answer: In an AI-agent economy, each participant must sustain a unique computational thread that continuously generates proofs of work linked to a private seed, similar to cracking a walnut's hard shell which requires sustained force. A Sybil attacker launching a gale of fake identities faces escalating costs because each thread consumes dedicated CPU cycles that cannot be shared or reused, and the network rejects any that fail to respond within tight windows, making mass forgery prohibitively expensive in energy and time.
